title: Crash when loading large meshes
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.4rc1 and 4.3 stable.

### System information

Godot v4.4.rc1 - Windows 11 (build 22631) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6614) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900K (32 threads)

Same happens with Forward+ rendering.

### Issue description

Large multi-mesh exports from Unreal will crash Godot. The export will load flawlessy in Threejs: https://gltf-viewer.donmccurdy.com/

If I decrease the number of meshes substantially, then the loading is successful in Godot as well. 

### Steps to reproduce

I export a scene from unreal to glb or gltf with heavily compressed textures and simplified materials - no translucency, metallic, animation etc. The export does include only meshes and the landscape. The file loads as expected in threejs in under 10 sec: https://gltf-viewer.donmccurdy.com/. The scene I export is the demo scene from https://www.fab.com/listings/1fbd637d-f56e-4ca1-8bdb-82c7183bb530

Given that it loads even in the browser, I'd think that Godot with a superior performance should be capable of performing the same import process.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

I export only the SM files, the landscape and the foliage from this project's demo scene:
https://www.fab.com/listings/1fbd637d-f56e-4ca1-8bdb-82c7183bb530

I use the following export settings in Unreal:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e71040ce-3c37-4336-b87d-239b132a8c19)

The engine crashes in a matter of seconds with Compatibility and Forward+ rendering as well.

Proof of the three js gltf loader working, no console errors either:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5499e9dc-f9a1-43f4-a2bd-66623eee7387)
